signals.entity: NBU / Ukrainian bank & CIT device estate
signals.signal: CONFIRMED device-configuration scope for the new 2000 UAH banknote: as of 01/06/2026 Ukraine operated 38,690 self-service devices - 15,750 ATMs and 22,930 PTKS (self-service payment kiosks). NBU said in August 2026 it would give market participants FREE technical capability to reconfigure note counters, sorters, authenticity detectors, ATMs and terminals; first time NBU has run a pre-launch device-configuration procedure. Note is 75x166mm, 6mm LONGER than the 1000 UAH note, so standard ATM cassettes must be physically replaced.
signals.implies: An estate-wide, hard-deadline cash-hardware event: NCR/Glory/Sesami cassette + firmware upgrades, cash-recycler recalibration, and 500+-engineer field-service mobilisation across 38,690 devices. Also an APTRA OptiCash re-optimisation trigger (a new highest denomination changes cassette mix and replenishment economics).
signals.followup: After 04/09/2026 chase which banks/PTKS operators still cannot accept the note - the laggards are the field-service and cassette-retrofit pipeline.

signals.signal: RE-VERIFIED against the primary text (published 18/06/2026, in force 26/06/2026): Resolution No.67 of 16/06/2026 does NOT simply ban anonymous PTKS top-ups - new clause 124-2 of Instruction No.103 requires, for EVERY cash-in at a PTKS regardless of amount, that the payer enter their FULL mobile number on the kiosk screen and that the PSP verify ownership of that number by a one-time password sent by SMS or read out by voice call; clause 124-3 obliges PSPs to continuously reduce OTP-sharing risk including shortening OTP validity. Exempted: taxes/fines/budget payments, utilities under the Housing-Services Law, fixed telephony/TV/internet/security, and rail (incl. suburban) tickets. Resolution also creates cash-work rules for the new 'financial-inclusion bank' licence type.
signals.implies: Every one of the ~22,930 PTKS kiosks needs a UI + OTP-flow software change and an SMS/voice-OTP integration: direct work for kiosk software, x-core-style device software, TMS-driven remote update, plus INETCO transaction monitoring and IMTF Siron/FICO AML rules to police OTP-sharing (mule) risk that clause 124-3 explicitly makes the PSP's duty.
signals.followup: Ask PTKS operators (EasyPay, iBox, City24) how they implemented the OTP step and whether NBU has begun enforcement.

signals.signal: Multi-year structural series now assembled from NBU annual/period releases: POS terminals in trade & service 496.6k (end-2024) -> 558.6k (end-2025, +12.5%, ~85% contactless) -> 563.4k (Mar-2026) -> 582.5k (Jun-2026). Card-accepting points of sale 459.7k (01/01/2024) -> 518.4k (01/01/2025) -> 614.1k (end-2025, +18.5%) -> 654.5k (Mar-2026) -> 699.3k (Jun-2026, +13.9% YTD). ATMs FLAT: 15.7k through 2024, 15.7k through 2025, 15.7k Mar-2026, 15.8k Jun-2026. Cards issued 132.0m (01/01/2025) -> 148.7m (01/01/2026) -> 153.2m (Jun-2026).
signals.implies: Sharp divergence: acceptance is growing ~13-19% a year (POS/softPOS/TMS pipeline) while the ATM estate is dead flat at 15.7-15.8k for three straight years. A flat estate with rising cash-handling demand is the classic cash-recycler business case (a recycler = an ATM that re-dispenses notes customers deposited, so one machine does the work of two) plus telemetry/monitoring and OptiCash cash-optimisation rather than new-footprint ATM sales.
signals.followup: Get the NBU 'Платіжна інфраструктура та платіжні картки' infographic files for the deposit-capable/recycler split, which the news text does not give.

signals.signal: eKYC/digital onboarding widened: NBU Resolution No.81 of 15/07/2026 (announced 16/07/2026, in force 17/07/2026) amends the Regulation on bank financial monitoring to expand permitted client identification/verification methods for financial-inclusion purposes - an original ID document may now be presented by a third party (companion/proxy) or handled by the verifying bank employee, and the client's consent to photo-capture may be given by AUDIO/VIDEO recording where a handwritten or electronic signature is impossible. The new 'financial-inclusion bank' licence type may delegate identification/verification and beneficial-owner determination to COMMERCIAL AGENTS. Existing remote routes (NBU BankID, qualified e-signature, Diia e-passport with DP Diia e-seal and qualified timestamp, video-verification) remain.
signals.implies: Agent-based and video/audio-consent onboarding is now legal: a direct fit for Namirial digital onboarding/e-signature (video-ID, audio/video consent capture, qualified timestamping) and for kiosk/tablet-based onboarding at agent points. The financial-inclusion-bank agent model also creates a NEW class of buyer (agent networks, post offices, retailers) needing onboarding devices and eKYC software rather than branches.
signals.followup: Track the first financial-inclusion bank licences and who supplies their agent-onboarding stack.

signals.signal: AML enforcement is biting: in July 2026 alone the NBU applied sanctions to 2 banks and 19 non-bank financial institutions. JSC 'BANK UKRAINSKYI KAPITAL' was fined UAH 40,545,000 for failure to properly organise primary financial monitoring - specifically an inadequate risk-based approach and risk-profile assessment, deficient internal AML documents, deficient customer due diligence, and failure to supply information to the inspection team. NBU also published (25/08/2026) an UPDATED 2026 on-site AML/currency/sanctions inspection plan, and an earlier amendment on 31/07/2026.
signals.implies: A UAH 40.5m fine for weak risk-scoring and CDD is a hard business case for IMTF Siron AML/KYC and FICO, plus INETCO transaction monitoring - and the 19 non-bank institutions hit are exactly the PSP/PTKS-operator population that must also implement the Resolution No.67 OTP rules. A published, updated inspection plan gives named prospects a dated compliance deadline.
signals.followup: Pull the updated 2026 inspection plan (25/08/2026) and match named institutions to AML/monitoring prospects.

signals.entity: NBU monetary statistics (M0 cash in circulation)
signals.signal: Cash is NOT shrinking in Ukraine despite a 96%-by-count cashless card share. Currency in circulation outside deposit-taking corporations (M0, UAH m, NBU statistics API): 581,011 (01/01/2022) -> 666,073 (01/01/2023) -> 716,167 (01/01/2024) -> 759,753 (01/01/2025) -> 866,944 (01/01/2026) -> 921,808 (01/08/2026). That is +14.1% during 2025 and a further +6.3% in the first seven months of 2026 - and it is precisely why the NBU is adding a 2000 UAH denomination.
signals.implies: Rising cash volumes handled by a FLAT 15.7-15.8k ATM estate = rising cost per note handled. This is the core cash-recycling / TCR business case (Glory, Sesami, NCR intelligent-deposit) plus NCR APTRA OptiCash cash-forecasting to cut CIT runs, and back-office cash automation in branches - the strongest structural argument Printec has in this market.
signals.followup: Get the deposit-capable/recycling share of the 15.8k ATM estate - NBU news text does not break it out.

signals.signal: [LEADING] monobank co-founder Oleh Horokhovskyi announced (via Threads, reported 31/08/2026) that the digital bank passed 11 million clients - a new record, from 10 million reported earlier. Momentum proxy for digital-channel adoption, not a structural device count. Context leading indicators: the state Diia app passed 24 million users in 2026 (~7m on the web portal), and NBU's own H1-2026 data shows tokenized cards at 21.1m (34.5% of active cards) and ~99% of in-store cashless volume contactless/NFC.
signals.implies: An 11m-client branchless bank on a flat ATM estate is the demand signal for softPOS/tap-to-phone acquiring, card issuing/management at scale, HSM & remote key injection for token/PIN volumes, and third-party cash-in points (PTKS/recyclers) as its only physical cash touchpoint.
signals.followup: Verify against Universal Bank's audited client/card counts and NBU banking-sector review.
